text: The applicant organisation is a non-governmental human rights organisation.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant organisation is based in Yerevan.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 12 May 2007, a third person identified as L.G. died while at a police station.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: L.G. was apparently a witness in a murder investigation at the time of his/her death.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the official version, L.G. died in an attempt to escape by jumping out of a second-floor window of the police station.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The death of L.G. on 12 May 2007 provoked an outcry among Armenian human rights groups and civil society.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 19 February 2008, a presidential election was held in Armenia.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The presidential election of 19 February 2008 in Armenia was followed by mass post-election rallies and protests.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The post-election rallies and protests resulted in an intense standoff between the Armenian authorities and the supporters of the opposition.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The standoff between the Armenian authorities and opposition supporters resulted in clashes.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The clashes following the 19 February 2008 presidential election in Armenia resulted in at least ten persons being killed.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 1 March 2008, a state of emergency was declared by the President of Armenia.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The state of emergency declared on 1 March 2008 by the President of Armenia was for a period of 20 days.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: During the state of emergency declared on 1 March 2008, all public assemblies in Armenia were banned.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 6 May 2008, the applicant organisation applied to the Mayor of Yerevan, notifying its intention to hold a mourning march on the first anniversary of L.G.'s death.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The mourning march notified by the applicant organisation was planned to take place on 12 May 2008.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The mourning march notified by the applicant organisation was planned to take place from 8 p.m. to 9.30 p.m.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The mourning march notified by the applicant organisation was planned to start at Republic Square in Yerevan.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The mourning march notified by the applicant organisation was planned to continue through Nalbandyan Street in the direction of the police station.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 8 May 2008, the Mayor of Yerevan decided to ban the planned mourning march.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Mayor of Yerevan's decision to ban the planned mourning march was made with reference to Section 9 § 4 (3) of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Mayor of Yerevan's decision to ban the planned mourning march was made with reference to Section 13 § 1 (3) of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Mayor of Yerevan's ban decision cited an official opinion of the Police dated 8 May 2008, stating that the mass public event held on 1 March 2008 turned into mass disorder resulting in human casualties.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Mayor of Yerevan's ban decision cited the Police opinion stating that not all the circumstances of the crime and offenders from the 1 March 2008 event had been disclosed.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Mayor of Yerevan's ban decision cited the Police opinion stating that not all weapons and ammunition used at the 1 March 2008 event, whose circulation may pose danger to the lives and health of citizens, had been found in the course of the investigation.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The investigation into the 1 March 2008 events was instituted by the Special Investigative Service of Armenia.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Mayor of Yerevan's ban decision cited the Police opinion concluding that it would be impossible to prevent new crimes if the planned mass public event were held.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Mayor of Yerevan's ban decision cited an official opinion of the National Security Service of Armenia dated 7 May 2008.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The National Security Service of Armenia's opinion of 7 May 2008 stated that the National Security Service had credible and verified data showing that the planned mass public event, if allowed, would result in undermining national security.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The National Security Service of Armenia's opinion of 7 May 2008 stated that the planned mass public event, if allowed, would result in undermining public order and the health and morality of society.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The National Security Service of Armenia's opinion of 7 May 2008 stated that the planned mass public event, if allowed, would result in encroachments on constitutional rights and freedoms.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The National Security Service of Armenia's opinion of 7 May 2008 stated that the planned mass public event, if allowed, would result in disorder and new crimes.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: By a letter dated 12 May 2008, the Mayor of Yerevan's ban decision of 8 May 2008 was posted to the applicant organisation.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 12 May 2008, the police prevented the organisers from holding the planned mourning march.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The police who prevented the organisers from holding the planned mourning march on 12 May 2008 had apparently been informed of the Mayor of Yerevan's ban decision of 8 May 2008.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 13 May 2008, the applicant organisation received the letter dated 12 May 2008 containing the Mayor of Yerevan's ban decision.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to Section 9 § 4 (3) of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the competent authority may ban the holding of a public event if, according to credible data, it is aimed at forcibly overthrowing the constitutional order.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 9 § 4 (3) of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the competent authority may ban the holding of a public event if, according to credible data, it is aimed at inflaming ethnic, racial or religious hatred.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 9 § 4 (3) of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the competent authority may ban the holding of a public event if, according to credible data, it is aimed at campaigning for violence or war.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 9 § 4 (3) of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the competent authority may ban the holding of a public event if, according to credible data, it may lead to mass disorder and crime.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 9 § 4 (3) of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the competent authority may ban the holding of a public event if, according to credible data, it may lead to undermining national security, public order and the health and morality of society.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 9 § 4 (3) of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the competent authority may ban the holding of a public event if, according to credible data, it may lead to encroachments on the constitutional rights and freedoms of others.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 9 § 4 (3) of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, data may be considered credible if the Police or the National Security Service under the Government of Armenia have issued an official opinion on the data.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 9 § 4 (3) of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the Police or the National Security Service under the Government of Armenia shall also issue an opinion if the grounds for banning cease to exist.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 9 § 4 (3) of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, an official opinion from the Police or the National Security Service under the Government of Armenia is also issued in cases envisaged by Section 9 § 6 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 9 § 6 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, in cases where mass public events have turned into mass disorder resulting in human casualties, the competent authority may temporarily ban the holding of mass public events in order to prevent new crimes.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 9 § 6 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the temporary ban on mass public events may be imposed only given that other means of prevention have been exhausted.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 9 § 6 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the temporary ban on mass public events shall last until the circumstances of the crime and the identity of the offenders have been disclosed.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 10 § 1 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, mass public events may be held only after notifying the competent authority in writing.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 10 § 4 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the organisers shall send written notification of the intention to hold a mass public event to the head of the local authority where the event is to be organised.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 10 § 4 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, if the public event is to be held in Yerevan, the written notification shall be sent to the Mayor of Yerevan.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 10 § 4 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the written notification shall be sent not later than five working days before the planned date of the event.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 10 § 4 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the written notification shall be sent not earlier than twenty days before the planned date of the event.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 12 § 1 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the competent authority shall examine the notification within 72 hours of receipt.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 12 § 1 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, notifications shall be examined in the order in which they have been received.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 12 § 6 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, in the absence of the circumstances mentioned in Section 13 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the notification of the mass public event shall be taken into consideration and the event shall be held in the place and at the time indicated in the notification.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 12 § 6 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, in the presence of the circumstances mentioned in Section 13 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, a decision shall be taken banning the mass public event.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 12 § 7 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the competent authority shall immediately inform the organisers of its decision taken as a result of examination of the notification.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 12 § 7 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the competent authority shall immediately inform the police of its decision taken as a result of examination of the notification.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 12 § 7 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the competent authority shall post up its decision on its premises in a specially designated spot, accessible and visible to the public.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 12 § 7 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the decision of the competent authority shall remain posted up until 6 p.m. on the planned date of the mass public event indicated in the notification.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 12 § 8 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, should the competent authority not take a decision banning the mass public event, the organisers shall have the right to hold the mass public event on the terms and conditions set forth in the notification.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 13 § 1 (3) of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, a mass public event may be banned only when, inter alia, there exist grounds stipulated by Section 9 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 13 § 2 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, a decision banning a mass public event shall contain a reasoned and clear explanation of the grounds on which the mass public event is banned.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 13 § 3 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, a decision banning a mass public event may be contested before the courts.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 13 § 3 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the court shall adopt a judgment within 24 hours of a challenge to a ban decision.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Section 13 § 3 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, a court judgment annulling a decision banning a mass public event shall enter into force from the moment of its delivery.
section_path: A. The Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act (as in force at the material time)

text: According to Articles 66-69 of the Code of Administrative Procedure, four types of application may be lodged with the Administrative Court.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Procedure

text: According to Article 66 of the Code of Administrative Procedure, an application to challenge may be lodged with the Administrative Court, seeking the annulment in part or in whole of the administrative act constituting an interference.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Procedure

text: According to Article 67 of the Code of Administrative Procedure, an application to oblige may be lodged with the Administrative Court, seeking the adoption of a favourable administrative act.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Procedure

text: According to Article 68 of the Code of Administrative Procedure, an application to perform an action may be lodged with the Administrative Court, seeking the performance of certain actions or refraining from certain actions.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Procedure

text: According to Article 69 of the Code of Administrative Procedure, an application to recognise may be lodged with the Administrative Court, seeking the recognition of existence or absence of a legal relationship.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Procedure

text: According to Article 69 of the Code of Administrative Procedure, an application to recognise may be lodged only if it is impossible to lodge an application under Articles 66-68 of the Code of Administrative Procedure.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Procedure

text: According to Article 69 of the Code of Administrative Procedure, an application to recognise may seek to recognise the invalidity of an administrative act.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Procedure

text: According to Article 69 of the Code of Administrative Procedure, an application to recognise may seek to recognise the unlawfulness of an interfering administrative act which is no longer in force, or of actions or inaction, if the applicant has a justified interest in doing so.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Procedure

text: According to Article 69 of the Code of Administrative Procedure, a justified interest in recognising the unlawfulness of an administrative act exists if there is a risk of adoption of a similar act or of performance of similar actions or inaction.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Procedure

text: According to Article 69 of the Code of Administrative Procedure, a justified interest in recognising the unlawfulness of an administrative act exists if the applicant intends to claim pecuniary damage.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Procedure

text: According to Article 69 of the Code of Administrative Procedure, a justified interest in recognising the unlawfulness of an administrative act exists if the applicant seeks to restore his honour, dignity or reputation.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Procedure
